narrative: A girl who was 12 when the Syrian uprising broke out in 2011. In 2013 her family fled their village in the Damascus countryside because of clashes between the army and armed opposition. Her older brother was detained and forcibly disappeared by Syrian security forces on New Year's Eve 2012, becoming one of the tens of thousands who vanished during the conflict. In January 2014 she and her mother witnessed regime forces detain and torture two of her uncles, who remain missing. By 2015, when she was 16, her aunt - the wife of an uncle who had been dragged behind a car - decided to flee to Germany with her seven children, and her parents decided she would go with the aunt, hoping the rest of the family could follow through family reunification. She left in September 2015. Fifteen days later she and her aunt reached Germany, after passing through Serbia, Macedonia, Bulgaria, Croatia and Austria. She hoped to bring her parents later, but her reunification request was denied: by the time the court ruled on her application she had turned 18 and held subsidiary protection rather than refugee status, which carries fewer rights. She has not seen her parents in seven years and has never met the little brother born a few months after she fled. She lives in Germany, graduated from high school there in 2022, and says Germany is her future, though Syria remains her homeland.
